decision: Daemon is one Rust binary (ds-daemon); all runtime state and hardware I/O live there (R1)
alternatives: Python daemon; Go daemon; multi-process microdaemons
why: No GIL under frame load; reuses mh-device/hidapi proven on this hardware; single static binary for systemd --user; team has Rust protocol knowledge in-repo
why_lost: Python: engine-thread blocking already observed (hubdeck/src/hubdeck/engine.py:465-514); Go: no existing device code, hidraw/libusb work redone; microdaemons: N sockets to secure, split-brain state

decision: CLI is a second Rust binary (ds) sharing a client crate with the daemon; one-shot per call, plus `ds watch` persistent mode
alternatives: Python CLI; shell functions; per-call state file read
why: Static binary starts in ~1-3 ms so one-shot beats interpreter startup (~30-50 ms); same code path as daemon client = no drift; `watch` covers long-lived subscriptions
why_lost: Python CLI: startup cost dominates p50 for tiny queries; state-file reads: no single writer, races with daemon

decision: Reuse upstream mh-protocol + mh-device as cargo dependencies (git dep), NOT a fork; deckstack licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 with NOTICE entry
alternatives: Fresh device layer; vendor (copy) the crates; fork
why: Crates are pure protocol + hidapi transport, already hardware-verified (safety-by-construction, timing); copying forks the moat; git dep keeps upstream fixes flowing; both licenses permissive
why_lost: Fresh layer: re-derives camera-verified facts (key grid, Huffman, 2.1 MB/s) and re-introduces brick risks; fork: maintenance split without benefit
evidence: upstream/Cargo.toml:8 license; crates/mh-protocol/src/safety.rs:8-32; upstream/PROTOCOL.md; task tension 6

decision: IPC: Unix socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/deckstack/daemon.sock (fallback ~/.local/state/deckstack/), NDJSON framing; Windows named pipe \\.\pipe\deckstack-<user>; optional WS/HTTP on 127.0.0.1 for UIs/agents
alternatives: Loopback TCP + port/token files (both current apps); plain files; D-Bus
why: Stable well-known path (no file discovery races — both apps' port-file discovery is racy, see discovery/20 §2); 0600 dir + scoped token; same framing code on both OSes via ds-ipc shim; loopback HTTP kept only as an opt-in adapter with Host check + bearer
why_lost: TCP+files: racy across users/installs, ephemeral ports (upstream engine/plugins.rs:336-358; hubdeck control.py:81-90); files: no backpressure, no auth; D-Bus: Linux-only, session-bus policy complexity

decision: State = one JSON document, path-addressed (/devices, /controls, /bindings, /plugins, /streams, /settings, /policy), global revision counter, optimistic transactions via if_rev, subscriptions per path glob; persisted atomically (temp+rename) to state.json
alternatives: Per-entity files; embedded SQLite; config-file-as-state (current hubdeck YAML)
why: Single owner (daemon), trivially queryable/serializable, diffs and subscriptions are easy; JSON matches R2 machine-readable; SQLite is a heavier dependency for a document this size
why_lost: SQLite: overkill, another on-disk format to reconcile; per-entity files: no cross-entity transactions, rename races; YAML config-as-state: hot-reload mtime polling was accidental complexity (hubdeck engine.py:469-472)

decision: Frames are bytes on a separate binary stream socket, never inside JSON state; per-module latest-frame-wins queue (1 in flight + 1 waiting) on a dedicated writer thread
alternatives: Frames in state JSON (base64); shm ring buffers; synchronous writes on control thread
why: Keeps the JSON query path fast and small (R2/R5); matches the proven upstream PictureSender; local socket throughput (~GB/s) dwarfs the 2.1 MB/s device cap so "local video" stays fast; portable to Windows pipes
why_lost: base64-in-JSON: ~33% bloat, GIL/lock pressure, blocks control; shm: not portable to named pipes, extra lifecycle; synchronous: observed to starve control (hubdeck engine.py:1325-1341)

decision: Action model: bindings are data in state; core vocabulary is exactly set/emit/plugin/exec/sleep/when; `exec` is argv-only (no shell) and requires the admin scope + per-binding opt-in; everything else is external programs subscribed to topics
alternatives: Hardcoded catalog (both current apps); python-in-yaml exec; shell-string actions
why: R3/R4/R8: anything displayable is reachable, behaviour composes via CLI, no eval, no closed catalog; daemon stays a router not an app
why_lost: Catalogs: upstream engine/actions.rs:105, hubdeck plugins/__init__.py:22-28 + schema.py:55-102 are the walled gardens being replaced; python-in-yaml exec at hubdeck plugins/python.py:58 violates R8; shell=True at platforms/posix.py:70 is the injection vector

decision: Plugins: one OS process per plugin, newline-JSON over stdio (or socketpair), manifest + JSON Schema params, per-plugin capability token, rlimits (nproc/nofile/as/cpu) + Landlock on Linux where available, watchdog respawn max 3/10 min
alternatives: In-process (hubdeck default); upstream WS-to-API-port with declared-but-unenforced permissions; containers
why: Process boundary gives real crash/resource isolation (R6/R8); stdio is the most portable transport (works on Windows pipes too); capability token makes grants explicit
why_lost: In-process: one plugin corrupts daemon state (hubdeck plugins/base.py); upstream model: permissions displayed only, "does not sandbox plugins" (upstream engine/plugins.rs:56-58); containers: heavy, not boring, Windows pain

decision: Python plugin compatibility via a wrapper process (ds-plugin-py) that speaks the ds plugin protocol and adapts the old hubdeck Plugin interface (actions/states/values, invoke/set) into manifest + effects
alternatives: Rewrite all Python plugins now; embed a Python interpreter in the daemon
why: Keeps the existing ecosystem reusable (R6) without in-process exec; wrapper guarantees process isolation and the wire contract, NOT deep API compatibility with engine internals
why_lost: Embedding CPython in daemon: R8 violation (in-process code); rewriting everything: throws away working plugins (huemux etc.)

decision: Repo topology: umbrella monorepo (this repo) with per-component crates; publish each component as its own repo via `git subtree split --prefix=<dir>`; contracts versioned in schemas/ with semver
alternatives: Git submodules; sibling repos from day one; single crate everything
why: Subtree split is one command per release, no submodule state to corrupt, components still edited atomically in one repo during development; contracts in-repo avoid cross-repo version skew; siblings rejected for phase 1 (contract churn needs one PR)
why_lost: submodules: hand-waving the task forbids, pointer drift; siblings: phase-1 contract churn across repos; single crate: violates R12 independent release

decision: Service model: `ds daemon start|stop|status` uses systemctl --user when available (shipped unit), else spawns detached with pidfile; fixed socket+token paths; guard child (stdin-pipe liveness) sends firmware handback on crash, max 3 restarts/10 min
alternatives: Manual-only start; socket-activation only; vendor-style tray app
why: Agents need deterministic start/stop/inspect (task tension 7); user service is the boring Linux answer; guard handback is proven upstream
why_lost: manual-only: agents can't reason about state; socket activation: systemd-only; tray: exactly the UI-coupled shape being replaced

decision: Linux-first (Bazzite/KDE/Wayland) with a ds-platform shim crate; core assumes nothing POSIX: sockets via ds-ipc, focus/media/keys via external sender binaries
alternatives: Windows-first; platform ifdefs scattered in daemon; X11-only tooling baked in
why: R9: Linux is primary; shim keeps one cfg boundary; external senders mean the core needs no watcher at all (R4); X11-only active-win-pos-rs (upstream engine/foreground.rs:157-195) is explicitly not baked in
why_lost: Windows-first: wrong primary target; scattered ifdefs: upstream has cfg(target_os) in ~35 files, that is the drift to avoid; baked-in X11 watcher: fails R9 on Wayland

decision: Query budget under 32 fps frame load: p50 <= 2 ms, p99 <= 10 ms, measured by the bench harness on the virtual device; achieved by frame I/O on separate writer threads with bounded queues and a state lock never held across I/O
alternatives: Larger budgets; client-side caching; faster language alone
why: Frame plane and state plane share no lock across I/O (D06); budget is asserted in CI, not aspirational (R2/R11); no benchmarks exist in either repo today, so the harness must reproduce the Python stall first to prove sensitivity
why_lost: Both current apps lack query-under-load benchmarks (discovery/50 F4); Python stall: hubdeck engine.py:465-514, 1325-1341

decision: Security posture: local-only default, per-install token with scopes read|mutate|admin, socket dir 0700 + token file 0600, no eval, exec only via admin scope + argv, image caps (16 MB wire, 4096x4096 decode, <=300 frames), plugin caps + rlimits + Landlock, HTTP adapter requires Host 127.0.0.1/localhost AND bearer
alternatives: Per-run tokens; no scopes; trust local processes; shell actions by default
why: R8 threat model; per-run tokens break stateless CLI across daemon restarts (upstream/D04); S1-S6 in discovery/50 are real: exec-in-config, shell=True, unsandboxed plugins, image bombs, path traversal, DNS rebinding
why_lost: Per-run token: hubdeck control.py:51 (per-run); no scope split: any token holder mutates everything incl. launch.run (control.py:101-123); trust-local: R8 says treat malicious config/plugins as real

decision: Video/display test answer (R5): the device has NO readback of screen content; proxy = host-side frames-sent log (bytes, chunks, timestamps, per-write return counts) + feature-read liveness (45-48 ms) + HID read errors as disconnect + optional camera oracle for golden frames; tests capture exactly that and the gap is documented
alternatives: Assume ack exists; USBPcap hunt for a feedback report; camera-only testing
why: No per-write ack exists and input reports carry only control events (discovery/40 §6, 50 T3); the proxy is the strongest available without hardware readback; camera rig stays out of CI
why_lost: Requiring readback: impossible as written — recorded in open-questions with the USBPcap experiment that would settle it; camera-only: non-deterministic, no CI

decision: Virtual device at the HID-report level (ds-vdev) injected at the transport boundary, reassembling chunked reports into frames and recording all writes; golden frames by sha256; black-box CLI conformance suite in Python driving the real ds binary
alternatives: Rust-only unit tests (upstream has no protocol-write harness); HUBDECK_AUTOMATION-style second full app copy
why: Python virtual hub already proves protocol-level assertions work (virtual_hub.py:17-130,196-246); black-box CLI tests satisfy R10; virtual device makes CI hardware-free
why_lost: Rust-only: misses report-level regressions (discovery/20 §9 OPEN confirmed); second-copy: tests the app, not the device contract

decision: Window watching is an external sender binary (ds-focus) that calls the CLI; core exposes only emit/subscribe; Linux backend: KWin D-Bus script first, wlr-foreign-toplevel fallback
alternatives: Watcher inside the daemon; Rust active-win-pos-rs poll baked in
why: R4 makes senders ordinary programs; neither current watcher has a native Wayland path (Python KWin-only hubdeck platforms/linux/focus.py:99-103; Rust X11/hyprland/kdotool upstream engine/foreground.rs:157-195) so the watcher must be swappable per DE anyway
why_lost: In-core: violates R4 and freezes one DE's mechanism into the daemon; active-win-pos-rs: X11-only on the primary target

decision: Home policy (Salon lights only) lives in state at /policy, enforced by the daemon on device-write requests, not hardcoded in core
alternatives: Policy in core; policy in each plugin; no policy
why: BRIEF: configuration/policy concern, not a core assumption — /policy is data any client can read and only admin can write; enforcement point is the single device-write choke point in the daemon
why_lost: Core-hardcoded: violates BRIEF's home-rule note; per-plugin: unenforceable and scattered

decision: Frame pushes never touch durable state or rev; stats sampled <=1 Hz into non-durable /telemetry (S1)
alternatives: stats in state with rev bump per frame; per-frame events
why: At 24-32 fps a rev bump + serialization per frame violates R2/R5 and floods subscribers
why_lost: bench asserts rev delta == 0 at 32 fps x 60 s (docs/30-testing.md §5)

decision: /bindings is an array of {id, topic, ...} objects, not path keys (S2)
alternatives: topics as flat path keys; escaped keys
why: Topics contain '/' and path addressing splits on '/'; flat keys are unreachable by ds get
why_lost: state.json bindings: array; cli.md bind returns bNNNN id

decision: No-shell is enforced: argv[0] absolute (schema) + /policy/exec/allow - /policy/exec/deny with shells/interpreters pre-denied; exec fire-and-forget, no timeout_ms (S3/S11, M1/M2)
alternatives: PATH lookup via /settings/exec_path; waiting on exec with timeout
why: /bin/sh -c passes any allowlist that only checks absoluteness; fire-and-forget removes the contradictory timeout semantics
why_lost: binding.json prefixItems ^/ + additionalProperties:false (no timeout_ms); conformance test asserts /bin/sh -c fails (docs/20-security.md T5)

decision: Plugin network is host-mediated (sdk.http -> request kind:net, daemon checks anchored host glob + /policy/net/allow_hosts); plugins never open sockets; Landlock net-deny where ABI>=4, gap documented otherwise (S4/M5)
alternatives: Landlock port rules; raw plugin sockets with glob caps
why: Landlock restricts ports not hostnames; glob semantics now defined: '*' = exactly one DNS label, anchored full-host match
why_lost: docs/contracts/plugins.md §2; T11 tests lights.lan.evil.com and a.b.lan vs *.lan

decision: Windows pipe + token files get explicit ACLs: pipe SDDL D:P(A;;GA;;;SY)(A;;GA;;;<user-sid>), files user+SYSTEM (S5)
alternatives: default pipe DACL
why: another local user can connect to a default-ACL pipe
why_lost: Windows CI/hw test with second account (docs/20-security.md T12)

decision: Stream target vocabulary unified to keys|key:N|dial; ds stream push = stream-open (NDJSON) + DSF1 binary on stream socket; stats/stop are NDJSON ops (S6/S14, B1/B2)
alternatives: separate --target flag with panel/screen synonyms; push as NDJSON op
why: one vocabulary removes grammar duplication; binary plane needs its own schema
why_lost: stream-frame.json; ipc.md §1.2 transport-per-verb table; fixtures validate

decision: Event ingest is transactional: app/focus/changed mirrors into /focus in the same transaction that dispatches bindings; when may read payload fields (S7)
alternatives: writer writes /focus separately; payload-only conditions
why: separate write races the binding evaluation
why_lost: conformance test in 30-testing.md §3; actions.md §2

alternatives: --json allowed on streaming verbs
why: ambiguous output contract

alternatives: 60 s grace for all requests; no rotation

decision: LED plane gets a latest-wins lane per LED target + a dedicated LED writer thread with one rate bucket per module (`/policy/led_rate_per_s` default 30/s, faders 25/s); report dedup (colour-only change = one 02 2D); rollers have no LED command so /controls/rollers/*/led is a one-shot warned no-op
alternatives: global 60/s bucket; try_acquire+pending on the device task; coalescing in the state task over the same bounded channel
why: newest colour always reaches the device with no stale backlog, and LED pacing can never block input reads or image pushes; a global raise is unsafe (faders dropped off USB at ~50/s); the bounded FIFO can still drop the newest push
why_lost: vdev bench tests/bench/led_latency.py --check: p95 18.9-19.5 ms, max 20.8 ms, 100/100 frames, 20 fps, 0 'no led report' over 4 runs; burst 200 writes -> newest 33.8 ms; ADR-018; crates/ds-daemon/src/led.rs; upstream/PROTOCOL.md:38,118-124

decision: DS-113: opt-in read-only localhost-only /preview debug surface (127.0.0.1 bind, bearer + loopback-Host T7, GET-only 405 on writes, WS read-only ops only, never any HID write) + action-metadata aggregate (schemas/action-metadata.json/v1 served at /preview/api/action-metadata); default-off via ds-daemon --preview flag or /policy/preview=true at boot, disableable live with /policy/preview=false
